newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Bolivian farmers end city vigil over land reforms.
newsitem.headline: Bolivian farmers end city vigil over land reforms.

text.p: Tens of thousands of Bolivian farmers left the capital city of La Paz on Sunday after a two-week protest against land reforms they said was futile.
"We're leaving, but the fight carries on," farmers' union leader Roman Loayza told reporters as some 10,000 farmers began a trek home of up to 400 miles (600 km).

The lower House of Congress approved the new land law on Friday and handed it to the Senate, where a ruling party majority is expected to pass it quickly. Loayza said most protesters were resigned to the fact that their demonstration was "to a great degree useless."

Last-minute amendments to the law, which is due to be debated on Tuesday by the Senate, allow the government to turn over fiscal property to local farming communities for free and only auction it off as a last resort.
Among other things the unions opposed the creation of a special agency in charge of enforcing environmentally-friendly farming techniques.

The law was also rejected by rural businessmen, who were granted a 50-percent tax cut but still called a "state of emergency" in the eastern district of Santa Cruz, accusing President Gonzalo Sanchez de Losada of failing to keep his promise to auction off fiscal land.
"Everyone is going to realize it's a good law," Sanchez de Losada said on Saturday as he left on a nine-day tour of Europe. "I rule for everyone, not just for businessmen."
